knowledge_point.title: Finding the Range of a Transformed Sinusoidal Function

question.:question/problem: What is the range of the function $y=4\cos(2x-3)-6$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The range of $\cos x$ is

$$
-1\le \cos x\le 1.
$$

Horizontal shifts and stretches have no effect on the range. Therefore,

$$
-1\le \cos(2x-3)\le 1.
$$

Multiplying the above inequality by $4$ and then subtracting $6$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & -1\le \cos(2x-3)\le 1 \\  & -4\le 4\cos(2x-3)\le 4 \\  & -10\le 4\cos(2x-3)-6\le -2 \\  & -10\le y\le -2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the range is $y\in [-10,-2].$

question.:question/problem: What is the minimum value of $f(x)=3\cos(x+90^{\circ})+2$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The range of $\cos x$ is

$$
-1\le \cos x\le 1.
$$

Horizontal shifts and stretches have no effect on the range. Therefore,

$$
-1\le \cos(x+90^{\circ})\le 1.
$$

Multiplying the above inequality by $3$ and then adding $2$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & -1\le \cos(x+90^{\circ})\le 1 \\  & -3\le 3\cos(x+90^{\circ})\le 3 \\  & -1\le 3\cos(x+90^{\circ})+2\le 5 \\  & -1\le f(x)\le 5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the minimum value is $-1.$

question.:question/problem: What is the minimum value of $f(x)=-\cos(4x+2)+4$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The range of $\cos x$ is

$$
-1\le \cos x\le 1.
$$

Horizontal shifts and stretches have no effect on the range. Therefore,

$$
-1\le \cos(4x+2)\le 1.
$$

Multiplying the above inequality by $-1$ and then adding $4$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & -1\le \cos(4x+2)\le 1 \\  & 1\ge -\cos(4x+2)\ge -1 \\  & 5\ge -\cos(4x+2)+4\ge 3 \\  & 3\le f(x)\le 5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the minimum value is $3.$

question.:question/problem: What is the minimum value of $f(x)=-6\sin(4x-3)+8$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The range of $\sin x$ is

$$
-1\le \sin x\le 1.
$$

Horizontal shifts and stretches have no effect on the range. Therefore,

$$
-1\le \sin(4x-3)\le 1.
$$

Multiplying the above inequality by $-6$ and then adding $8$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & -1\le \sin(4x-3)\le 1 \\  & 6\ge -6\sin(4x-3)\ge -6 \\  & 14\ge -6\sin(4x-3)+8\ge 2 \\  & 2\le f(x)\le 14.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the minimum value is $2.$

question.:question/problem: What is the range of the function $y=- \frac{5}{2}\cos(x-15^{\circ})-\frac{14}{3}$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The range of $\cos x$ is

$$
-1\le \cos x\le 1.
$$

Horizontal shifts and stretches have no effect on the range. Therefore,

$$
-1\le \cos(x-15^{\circ})\le 1.
$$

Multiplying the above inequality by $- \frac{5}{2}$ and then subtracting $\frac{14}{3}$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & -1\le \cos(x-15^{\circ})\le 1 \\  & \frac{5}{2}\ge - \frac{5}{2}\cos(x-15^{\circ})\ge - \frac{5}{2} \\  & - \frac{13}{6}\ge - \frac{5}{2}\cos(x-15^{\circ})-\frac{14}{3}\ge - \frac{43}{6} \\  & - \frac{43}{6}\le y\le - \frac{13}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the range is $y\in [- \frac{43}{6},- \frac{13}{6}].$

question.:question/problem: What is the range of the function $y=- \frac{7}{3}\sin(x+90^{\circ})+\frac{15}{4}$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The range of $\sin x$ is

$$
-1\le \sin x\le 1.
$$

Horizontal shifts and stretches have no effect on the range. Therefore,

$$
-1\le \sin(x+90^{\circ})\le 1.
$$

Multiplying the above inequality by $- \frac{7}{3}$ and then adding $\frac{15}{4}$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & -1\le \sin(x+90^{\circ})\le 1 \\  & \frac{7}{3}\ge - \frac{7}{3}\sin(x+90^{\circ})\ge - \frac{7}{3} \\  & \frac{73}{12}\ge - \frac{7}{3}\sin(x+90^{\circ})+\frac{15}{4}\ge \frac{17}{12} \\  & \frac{17}{12}\le y\le \frac{73}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the range is $y\in [\frac{17}{12},\frac{73}{12}].$

question.:question/problem: What is the minimum value of $f(x)=- \frac{5}{2}\cos(5x-2)-\frac{11}{2}$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The range of $\cos x$ is

$$
-1\le \cos x\le 1.
$$

Horizontal shifts and stretches have no effect on the range. Therefore,

$$
-1\le \cos(5x-2)\le 1.
$$

Multiplying the above inequality by $- \frac{5}{2}$ and then subtracting $\frac{11}{2}$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & -1\le \cos(5x-2)\le 1 \\  & \frac{5}{2}\ge - \frac{5}{2}\cos(5x-2)\ge - \frac{5}{2} \\  & -3\ge - \frac{5}{2}\cos(5x-2)-\frac{11}{2}\ge -8 \\  & -8\le f(x)\le -3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the minimum value is $-8.$

question.:question/problem: What is the range of the function $y=- \frac{4}{3}\sin(4x+\frac{\pi}{6})+\frac{14}{3}$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The range of $\sin x$ is

$$
-1\le \sin x\le 1.
$$

Horizontal shifts and stretches have no effect on the range. Therefore,

$$
-1\le \sin(4x+\frac{\pi}{6})\le 1.
$$

Multiplying the above inequality by $- \frac{4}{3}$ and then adding $\frac{14}{3}$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & -1\le \sin(4x+\frac{\pi}{6})\le 1 \\  & \frac{4}{3}\ge - \frac{4}{3}\sin(4x+\frac{\pi}{6})\ge - \frac{4}{3} \\  & 6\ge - \frac{4}{3}\sin(4x+\frac{\pi}{6})+\frac{14}{3}\ge \frac{10}{3} \\  & \frac{10}{3}\le y\le 6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the range is $y\in [\frac{10}{3},6].$

question.:question/problem: What is the range of the function $y=- \frac{9}{2}\sin(3x+\pi)-\frac{10}{3}$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The range of $\sin x$ is

$$
-1\le \sin x\le 1.
$$

Horizontal shifts and stretches have no effect on the range. Therefore,

$$
-1\le \sin(3x+\pi)\le 1.
$$

Multiplying the above inequality by $- \frac{9}{2}$ and then subtracting $\frac{10}{3}$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & -1\le \sin(3x+\pi)\le 1 \\  & \frac{9}{2}\ge - \frac{9}{2}\sin(3x+\pi)\ge - \frac{9}{2} \\  & \frac{7}{6}\ge - \frac{9}{2}\sin(3x+\pi)-\frac{10}{3}\ge - \frac{47}{6} \\  & - \frac{47}{6}\le y\le \frac{7}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the range is $y\in [- \frac{47}{6},\frac{7}{6}].$
